endorsements.quote: For transparency, state insurance departments or CMS should require insurers to publicly disclose their PA practices, inclusive of denial and appeal rates.

unlisted_practices: CMS should require algorithm transparency measures, similar to the ASTP/ONC HTI-1 Final Rule, for AI used in prior authorization and coverage determinations.

CMS should name or appoint a certification entity, structured as a public-private partnership or private group akin to JCAHO, to develop and implement standards for AI use in prior authorization and coverage determinations.

Insurers should prominently disclose to current and prospective Medicare Advantage beneficiaries their prior authorization rates, denial rates, peer-to-peer review rates and durations, and appeal rates.
State regulators should guide payers on appropriate uses of prior authorization and AI in the prior authorization process for complex care cases.

State insurance departments or CMS should disincentivize or eliminate complex prior authorization processes involving extensive peer-to-peer reviews with peers who are unqualified or untrained in the relevant clinical area.
State insurance departments or CMS should develop guidance on the appropriate number of prior authorization requests and time spent on peer-to-peer or other reviews.

Regulators should cap or limit prior authorization requests, or penalize high prior authorization denial rates, to reduce automatic batch denials and encourage careful review of complex, time-sensitive cases.

State regulators should work with CMS to create or redesign a database to monitor and report prior authorization approval and denial patterns and surveil patterns of discrimination, including the effects of gold card programs on vulnerable patients.
Regulators should incentivize Medicare Advantage plans to adopt AI that accounts for the latest reliable evidence and individual patient health history during prior authorization.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/perspective article discussing issues with AI-assisted prior authorization denials in Medicare Advantage plans and calling for improved transparency and governance.
